exposure: Four groups based on preference for and actual mode of delivery: Match 1 (no preference for cesarean section, no elective cesarean section), Match 2 (preference for cesarean section, elective cesarean section), Mismatch 1 (no preference for cesarean section, elective cesarean section), and Mismatch 2 (preference for cesarean section, no elective cesarean section).
mismatch between preferred and actual mode of delivery
cohort: 1,700 women scheduled to give birth between 2009 and 2010 at Akershus University Hospital, Norway
finding: Women who preferred delivery by cesarean section but delivered vaginally had increased post-traumatic stress symptoms compared to women who both preferred vaginal delivery and delivered vaginally.
mod_finding: Women who preferred a cesarean section but delivered vaginally had significantly higher levels of post-traumatic stress symptoms compared to women who both preferred and had a vaginal delivery.
